CIEN.thesis_one_line: The top independent optical-networking supplier riding the AI-datacenter-interconnect boom, but the stock already prices in a decade of today's exceptional growth rate.
kill_criteria: Quarterly revenue growth decelerates below 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters
RPO ($2.5bn as of Aug 1 2026) declines quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters
Net debt (gross LT debt minus cash) exceeds $2.5bn
Any single 'cloud provider' customer disclosed (or inferable from segment concentration commentary) at >15% of revenue
A guidance cut (vs. the immediately prior quarter's range)
key_adverse_facts: Management itself discloses rising customer concentration: 'a small number of those customers become a larger portion of our business' across multiple revenue segments (10-Q MD&A, Q3 FY26)
Nine-month FY26 capex was $194.9m vs $95.4m a year earlier (+104%), pressuring near-term FCF even as revenue grows
June 2026 $2.875bn 0% convertible note issuance roughly doubled reported debt and cash simultaneously; a reader of the balance sheet without the notes could misread this as distress

Trailing GAAP P/E ~79x and implied 10-year FCF CAGR of ~21-23% as first built (DV09 restated to ~25-30% after deducting stock-based compensation from FCF and tying the discount rate to the 5.17% Treasury) leave little valuation cushion for any normalization of the AI-capex cycle
data_conflicts: None material found between filings and the quant snapshot; the step-change in cash/debt between the Q2 and Q3 FY26 10-Qs is fully explained by the June 2026 convertible offering (Note 13), not a data error
CIEN.confidence_in_thesis: medium (durable AI-interconnect demand is well evidenced by RPO and 3 straight guidance raises, but sustaining a ~25-30% 10-year FCF CAGR (DV09-restated; first built at ~21%+) is a high bar and next_earnings_date is an estimate pending the actual Q4 FY26 8-K)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CIEN in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict is null; the analyst's own reverse-FCF-DCF puts the implied 10-year growth (~21-23% as built; DV09 restated ~25-30% once SBC is deducted from FCF and the rate is consistent with the 5.17% Treasury) above an evidence-based base case (~15%), consistent with a 'full' valuation view and the WATCH verdict.

CIEN.scenario_basis: Starting point NTM consensus EPS $9.93 (d4 snapshot); bear = 5%/yr EPS growth with multiple compression to 18x NTM P/E (AI-capex cycle normalizes hard); base = 20%/yr EPS growth with multiple compression to 28x (cycle moderates but persists); bull = 30%/yr EPS growth holding ~35x (current NTM multiple, cycle sustains); no dividend.

COHR.thesis_one_line: A photonics and laser leader turning around into an AI-optics transceiver supplier, with three straight quarters of beat-and-raise, but free cash flow is still negative.
kill_criteria: FCF stays negative (OCF minus capex < $0) for two consecutive fiscal quarters after FY26 Q4
Quarterly revenue guidance is cut (below the immediately prior quarter's stated range)
Net debt/consolidated total debt rises above $4.0bn without a corresponding step-up in FCF guidance
Non-GAAP-to-GAAP EPS gap widens beyond 50% for two consecutive quarters
Organic revenue growth decelerates below 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: FY26 (ended Jun 30 2026) operating cash flow was only $79.5m against $1,102.9m of capex, i.e. FCF of approximately negative $1.02 billion for the year, despite the earnings recovery
Q4 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS was $1.19 vs non-GAAP $1.74, a roughly 46% gap driven by amortization, restructuring and SBC add-backs
The business remains exposed to the same AI-optics customer-concentration and cyclicality risk as CIEN and LITE
data_conflicts: None material found; the FCF-based reverse DCF could not be used directly because FCF is currently negative, so a non-GAAP-EPS-based reverse DCF was substituted and flagged as a softer estimate
COHR.confidence_in_thesis: medium (revenue acceleration and guidance-beat pattern are well evidenced by three quarters of primary filings, but the turnaround's cash-conversion is not yet proven, which is the reason for INCLUDE-SMALL rather than INCLUDE)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for COHR in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict is null; the analyst's reverse non-GAAP-EPS DCF implies a ~19-21% 10-year EPS CAGR, which is judged in_line with (not clearly above) an evidence-based base case of similar magnitude, consistent with a 'fair' dossier view.

COHR.scenario_basis: Starting point NTM consensus non-GAAP-style EPS $10.51 (d4 snapshot); bear = 8%/yr EPS growth with multiple compression to 15x (capex-heavy turnaround stalls, FCF stays negative); base = 20%/yr EPS growth with multiple compression to 24x (from current ~28x NTM P/E); bull = 28%/yr EPS growth holding ~30x (AI-optics supercycle plus successful capacity ramp); no dividend.

HOOD.thesis_one_line: A fast-growing retail brokerage expanding into options, crypto and prediction markets, priced for continued hypergrowth even though a bill to ban prediction markets is already in the Senate.
kill_criteria: Federal or state legislation materially restricting or banning prediction-market event contracts is enacted
Crypto-trading revenue declines YoY for a second consecutive quarter (already -38% YoY in Q2 2026)
Any regulated subsidiary's excess net capital falls below 2x its required minimum
Total Platform Assets or net deposits growth decelerates below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters
The $2.2bn convertible notes' conversion feature triggers material dilution disclosure, or a second convertible/equity raise occurs within 12 months
key_adverse_facts: A U.S. Senate bill (the 'Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act,' introduced March 23, 2026) would prohibit certain event contracts, directly targeting the fastest-growing revenue line
Illinois enacted a 1.75%/3.5% tax on prediction-market contract value effective July 1, 2026, a live example of state-level cost/revenue erosion that could spread
Cryptocurrency revenue fell 38% YoY in Q2 2026 on lower rebate rates and a 16-24% decline in users placing crypto trades
Operating cash flow is extremely volatile for a broker-dealer (H1 2025 OCF $4,151m vs full-year 2025 OCF only $1,638m) and is not a reliable free-cash-flow proxy for valuation purposes
data_conflicts: The quant snapshot's Yahoo-sourced 'totalDebt' (~$22.9bn) and 'totalCash' (~$23.9bn) reflect broker-dealer balance-sheet items (customer payables, securities-lending/repurchase obligations), not corporate funded debt; actual parent-level funded debt is the $2.2bn 0% convertible notes issued June 2026, with cash of $5.36bn against it

The snapshot's insider-ownership field (y_heldPercentInsiders ~0.96%) looks implausibly low for a founder-controlled company and is flagged as a likely vendor data-classification issue, not independently confirmed
HOOD.confidence_in_thesis: medium (the brokerage diversification and net-income growth are well evidenced by primary filings, but the regulatory risk to prediction markets is a live, dated, binary threat that could change the growth algebra quickly)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for HOOD in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict is null; the analyst's reverse net-income-based DCF implies a ~20-23% 10-year earnings CAGR, which is above an evidence-based base case (~15-18%), consistent with an 'expensive' dossier view and the WATCH verdict.

HOOD.scenario_basis: Starting point NTM consensus EPS $2.62 (d4 snapshot); bear = 10%/yr EPS growth with multiple compression to 18x (prediction markets curtailed, crypto softness persists) landing near the Street's own $57 low target; base = 25%/yr EPS growth with multiple compression to 30x landing near the Street's own $130 mean target; bull = 40%/yr EPS growth at 40x landing near the Street's own $170 high target; no dividend.
